forbid.name: queue_consumer:orders
forbid.note: MEASURED VIOLATION: `.QueueDeclare(` is a CONSUMER needle, so the producer's own `QueueDeclare(queue: "orders", ...)` (the RabbitMQ .NET tutorial's Send.cs shape) mints a second queue_consumer:orders in the server repo and QueueStackResolver pairs the producer with it -- two QUEUE_FLOWS edges, one a false self-flow. Declaring a queue is not consuming it. Same violation as matrix/python/amqp

note: A15.8 baseline 2026-09-17: PARTIAL -- extract 2/2, literal 2/2, route 1/1, forbid 2/3. The review's 'C# is accidentally partial' still holds in a new form: `.BasicConsume(` has NO needle, so the consumer is found only because the tutorial shape also calls `QueueDeclare` in the consumer -- a worker consuming a queue declared elsewhere reads none. Written against the v6 API the spec names (`IModel`); v7's `BasicPublishAsync` / `BasicConsumeAsync` / `QueueDeclareAsync` match no row at all. Keyed on QUEUE_* + QUEUE_FLOWS like every A15.7 messaging cell, including the eventbus-first mechanisms (sqs_sns, azure_sb, redis, mqtt), so TypeScript/Java/C# read on the same scale as Python/Go and an EVENT_* key cannot flip to `none` when A2.9 moves broker pub/sub out of eventbus.rs. `via` still records the eventbus path when that is what fired. Measured against the installed wheel at HEAD bc42921.
